appraisal_events.evidence: « Il croit qu'il a inventé la stratégie […] il emploie des mots impossibles pour les moindres choses, ce qui n'empêche pas qu'il fait des pâtés dans ses lettres […] des pommes de terre sublimes […] une baignoire sublime. » — « Il parle latin, enchérit le duc. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The duchesse ridicules the absent Saint-Loup as a pretentious pseudo-intellectual whose grand vocabulary is undercut by misuse and schoolboy blots, and the duc bids the mockery higher; the dinner table is turned into an audience for his diminishment.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Justement c'est à propos du Maroc… s'écria la princesse saisissant précipitamment ce joint. — Qu'est-ce qu'il peut vouloir pour le Maroc ? demanda sévèrement M. de Guermantes ; Oriane ne peut absolument rien dans cet ordre-là, il le sait bien. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The princesse's attempt to place Saint-Loup's request is cut off severely before she can state it, and the narrator's tag ('saisissant précipitamment ce joint') marks her as grasping at an opening; she is left supplying naive feed lines ('Comment, latin ?') to the couple's routine.

status_effects.explanation: He is comprehensively ridiculed in absentia for pretension, misused words, and bad spelling, with no one in the scene defending him.
His solicited favour is refused before it is even formulated ('Oriane ne peut absolument rien dans cet ordre-là'), so his claim on the Guermantes' credit is locally denied.
Her mockery holds the table: the duc seconds and escalates it ('enchérit') and the princesse's questions solicit more of it, confirming her as the salon's authoritative wit.
Despite her rank she is spoken to severely, her intercession is deflected, and she is reduced to the role of straight man asking for explanations.

ambiguities: The passage never names the mocked man; 'il' is read here as Robert de Saint-Loup on the strength of the immediately adjacent context (the princesse's request on behalf of 'votre neveu Saint-Loup' just before, and 'mais Robert a jeté cela sans reprendre haleine' just after). If 'il' were read otherwise, all Saint-Loup effects would fall away.

'la princesse' matches the reference sheet's alias list for the princesse de Guermantes, but in this dinner scene the speaker addressed as 'Votre Altesse' is the princesse de Parme, named as such a few paragraphs earlier; the resolution to Parme is committed but rests on adjacent context rather than on the passage itself.
